steps: Identify: is it a tangent, chord, diameter, or radius?
Look for angle at centre vs circumference
Cyclic quad: opposite angles sum to 180°
method_card.title: Circle Theorems
method_card.content: Key theorems: (1) Angle at centre = 2× angle at circumference. (2) Angle in a semicircle = 90°. (3) Angles in the same segment are equal. (4) Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral sum to 180°. (5) Tangent is perpendicular to radius. (6) Alternate segment theorem. (7) Two tangents from external point are equal.
method_card.example:
Angle at centre = 120°. Find the angle at the circumference subtended by the same arc.

120° ÷ 2 = 60°.

gold.display: Prove: angle at centre = 2 × angle at circumference. If circumference angle = \(3x + 5\) and centre angle = \(8x - 10\), find \(x\).
A cyclic quadrilateral has angles \(3x\), \(4x\), \(5x\), and \(6x\). Find \(x\).

misconceptions.message: Sum = 360°: 18x = 360 → x = 20. Check opposite: 3(20)+5(20)=160≠180. Hmm — actually opposite must sum to 180: 3x+5x=180→8x=180→x=22.5. But also 4x+6x=180→10x=180→x=18. Contradiction — so the angles must just sum to 360°: x = 20.

gold.display: A tangent at T and chord TA. Angle between tangent and TA = 48°. Angle ATB (B on circle, same side) = ?

misconceptions.message: Alternate segment theorem: angle in alternate segment = 48°.

gold.display: Two chords AB and CD intersect at P inside a circle. PA = 3, PB = 8, PC = 4. Find PD.

misconceptions.message: Intersecting chords: PA × PB = PC × PD. 3 × 8 = 4 × PD → PD = 6.

gold.display: A tangent from P touches at T. A secant from P passes through A and B on the circle. PT = 12, PA = 8. Find PB.

bronze.display: Angle at centre = 100°. Angle at circumference?

misconceptions.message: Angle at circumference = ½ × angle at centre = 50°.

misconceptions.message: Angles in the same segment are equal = 42°.

bronze.display: Cyclic quadrilateral: angle A = 80°. Find angle C (opposite).
Angle at centre = 160°. Angle at circumference (same arc)?
Angle in a semicircle plus another angle = 180°. The other angle in the triangle is 50°. Find the remaining angle.

silver.display: Cyclic quad: angles are \(2x\), \(3x\), \(2x+20\), and \(y\). Opposite pairs sum to 180°. Find \(x\) if \(2x\) and \(2x+20\) are opposite.
A tangent makes an angle of 55° with a chord. Find the angle in the alternate segment.
Two tangents from an external point. One tangent makes 70° with the line to centre. Find the angle between the two tangents.

misconceptions.message: Each tangent-radius = 90°. Angle at centre = 180° − 2(70°) = 40°. Wait: if tangent makes 70° with line to centre, angle between tangents = 2×70° − 90°? Let me reconsider. In the kite, angles: 90°, 90°, angle at centre, angle at point. 360° = 90+90+centre+point. If 70° is angle between tangent and line to centre at the point, then angle at point = 2×70° = 140°. Centre = 360−90−90−140 = 40°.

silver.display: Angle at centre is reflex: 260°. Find the angle at circumference (same arc, minor).
Two tangents from point P. PA = 8 cm. What is PB?

misconceptions.message: Two tangents from same point are equal. PB = 8 cm.

silver.display: Angle at circumference = \(x\), angle at centre = \(3x - 20\). Find \(x\).
In a semicircle, angle BAC = 90°, angle ABC = 28°. Find angle ACB.
